summary: After graduating from a double degree in Engineering, I began working for a medium-size engineering company in England, Stirling Dynamics.
I provided engineering support to various customers in the aerospace and energy sectors, such as Airbus UK, BAe Systems, BNFL.
More than the start of my profesionnal career, it was an enriching human experience within a diverse group of engineers.
As an employee of Aeroconseil Iberica, I have worked full time onsite for our main customer, Airbus Spain.
I worked on the New Empenage For Aircraft (NEFA) R&D program.
Not only did I improve my knowledge in aerodynamic and mathematical modelling, but I also took the opportunity to learn spanish and use it on a daily basis.
As a freelancer/contractor, I performed aerodynamic calculations for the Flight Physics Department within Airbus Germany.
Since it was only a 4-month contract, this taught me to work efficiently and deliver analysis and reporting under time pressure.
While I was running aerodynamic simulations during my first years, I noticed the need to automate our processes and progressivly taught myself Software development accordingly.
In particular, I started improving our aerodynamic analysis and pre- and post-processes by developing a Graphical User Interface (GUI).
Within the CFD department, this platform has now become the standard tool for analysing simulation results.
Guided by my growing passion for Software Development, I changed position internally in 2017 to fully embrace this field.
My main focus are test and simulation data analysis, DataViz using GUIs and Dashboards, as well as simulation lifecycle management between multi-physic disciplines.
In particular, I commit myself to pushing our team towards a better UX Design, cleaner and better architecture, and more intuitive Visualization tools.
